board.name: Five Independent Directors (including one woman director)

drhp.business: KM Sugar Mills manufactures sugar from sugarcane and operates an integrated business model that converts by-products into valuable resources. The company produces surplus power from bagasse-based co-generation sold to the state grid, and has a wholly-owned subsidiary, KM Spirits and Allied Industries Limited, incorporated to manufacture all types of spirits, though it is yet to commence operations. The company sells sugar primarily on cash terms, and ethanol and power to government undertakings.

risks.note: The sudden demise of founder promoter L.K. Jhunjhunwala (ceased 14.03.2026) and subsequent appointment of promoter-group member Naina Devi Jhunjhunwala as Additional Director (18.05.2026) introduces uncertainty in strategic supervision and family control dynamics.
risks.risk: Promoter succession and board stability risk

risks.note: Promoter and promoter group hold 56.51% of shares. Material related-party transactions continue, including Rs 2350 Lacs investment in OFCDs of K M Strategic Investments & Holding Pvt Ltd and a corporate guarantee of Rs 6174.21 lacs plus Rs 375 Lacs preference share investment in Sonar Castings Limited, creating potential conflict and capital-allocation risk.
risks.risk: Concentrated promoter-group control and related-party exposure

risks.note: Both the sugar unit and distillery unit are located in District Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, exposing the company to region-specific agro-climatic, regulatory, and logistical disruptions.

As a sugar mill with a distillery unit, the company's performance is structurally tied to cane availability, government-set sugarcane pricing, sugar release mechanisms, and ethanol blending policies, which are outside management control.

The board includes an Independent, Executive Director-cum-CEO (S.C. Agarwal) responsible for strategic management and implementation, creating reliance on a single non-promoter executive for day-to-day leadership.

The Audit Committee includes one promoter executive director as member alongside two independent directors; the board has three promoter executive directors out of eight, and inter-se family relationships dominate the promoter bloc, potentially diluting independent oversight.
risks.risk: Limited board and committee independence in practice
